title: #498: This is the Way! Reality Fracture Early Limited Guide

format.summary: The hosts call it an all-time great, high-synergy, high-power, high-complexity format that plays like a cube, with many viable lanes. Power is concentrated in rares and uncommons, especially appropriately pipped gold uncommons and the Way enchantments. Empower Jace creates rich decisions in both draft and sealed, and sealed pools are complex and swingy.
format.speed: Slow and grindy when both players curve out and play removal: games reach seven- and eight-drops and decks are mana hungry. You still must affect the board early and interact, and boards see lots of trading rather than pure stalls.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: A clean, great mechanic that matters much more in draft than in sealed. It works fine with two instances and gets better with ten plus Way cards. Don't auto-activate tokens, because sitting at one loyalty can be right, and attack opposing Jace tokens aggressively.

mechanics.name: Way of enchantments
mechanics.take: The meat of the format. The cheap ones (Pyromancer, Paradox, Deathbringer, Healer, Cryomancer) are rate monsters, while Warlord and Mind Sculptor are less efficient. Pyromancer, Necromancer and Mentor need an existing Jace token to tick it up.

mechanics.name: Prepared spells (Seed Suture, Peer Review, Heartwood, Vicious Verse, Omit Variables)
mechanics.take: A clever way to seed synergy, but let those decks come to you. Seed Suture, Peer Review and Heartwood are better than Vicious Verse and Omit Variables, and Omit Variables did occasionally enable stacking your library in long games.

mechanics.name: Land cyclers
mechanics.take: Much bigger in sealed; in draft they are mostly filler because splashing is hard and many cards are double-pipped.

mechanics.name: Mirrored pairs
mechanics.take: They can create very high-powered sealed pools and make pod power levels vary.

advice: Prioritize raw power and rare/uncommon hooks; don't let commons steer your draft.
Take the best card in the first four or five packs and stay open, drafting 'the hard way' rather than forcing a color.
Avoid half-baked synergy decks, especially Vicious Verse noncombat damage, unless the lane is clearly open.
Value mana sinks, card filtering and repeatable late-game advantages because games go long.
Don't activate every Jace token automatically; consider holding at one loyalty for Way uptick effects.
Attack opposing Jace tokens off the board unless you are hyper-aggressive.
Once you commit to a synergy, supporting commons like Inspired Tethermage rise sharply in value.
Removal is premium; don't end up removal-light.
